Object Interaction Layer.Specific Description: Vehicle 1 was following Vehicle 2 too closely, as the driver of Vehicle 2 observed Vehicle 1 approaching at a 'high rate of speed and knew he (V1) wouldn't be able to stop in time.' This insufficient following distance was a critical factor in the rear-end collision.

There was a large longitudinal speed difference between Vehicle 1 (traveling at or around the speed limit) and Vehicle 2 (decelerating for congestion). This discrepancy made it difficult for Vehicle 1 to react in time to the slowing traffic, as stated in the report: âVehicle #1 was still traveling at or around the speed limit when other traffic began to slow downâ.

Vehicle 1 engaged in emergency braking and a swerving maneuver to avoid traffic, indicating a late reaction to the sudden deceleration of traffic ahead. The report states, 'The driver of V1 also realizing traffic was slowing significantly swerved left to avoid traffic and struck V2 in the back end.'

Environment Layer.Specific Description: The crash occurred under rainy and wet conditions, leading to a slippery road surface and reduced braking effectiveness. Based on the report, 'The crash occurred in the morning rush hour under rainy and wet conditions.'

Adverse weather including rain occurred around the time of the incident, likely impacting visibility. While not explicitly stated to be poor, rain restricts visibility. The report states, 'The crash occurred in the morning rush hour under rainy and wet conditions.'

Other Relevant Risk Layer.Specific Description: The left front tire of Vehicle 1 had only 3mm of tread, potentially reducing its grip and contributing to the difficulty in stopping. The report noted, 'A potential Vehicle Related Factor is that the left front tire was smaller than the other three and had only 3mm of tread on it.'

The driver of Vehicle 1 acknowledged looking down to get coffee immediately before the crash, leading to a 'Recognition Error' and a delayed reaction to the slowing traffic. As reported, 'I looked down to get my coffee and when I looked up every one was stopping'.

The driver of Vehicle 1 was potentially fatigued, having been awake for over 4.5 hours and having had only 6 hours of sleep the night before, contributing to the recognition error. The report states, 'The driver of V1 may have been fatigued since he got up at 3AM and had been up for over 4 1/2 hours already.'
